experiment_plans.feasibility_notes: Synthetic point cloud, k-means, trivially cheap.
experiment_plans.objective: Test whether k-means recovers known cluster structure better than random assignment at increasing overlap.
experiment_plans.design: Cluster analysis across three separation levels, each compared to a random-assignment control.

data_requirements.description: Three Gaussian blobs in two dimensions with configurable separation and known ground-truth labels.
preprocessing_steps: Generate blobs at each separation level with a fixed seed

methods.name: k-means clustering
methods.description: Lloyd's algorithm with k fixed to the known number of clusters.

evaluation.baseline: Random assignment of points to the same number of clusters.
evaluation.success_criteria: k-means beats random assignment on adjusted Rand index at every separation level tested.

risks: At the lowest separation the clusters may be genuinely unrecoverable.

priority_order.justification: the only plan in this benchmark case
